rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists several activities that all belong to one stage, have no stated order between them, and a later step waits until every one of them has finished: Model each listed activity as its own task. Open the branches with a parallel gateway placed before the first of these tasks, and close them with a matching parallel gateway placed before the next step. Do not sequence the tasks unless the description states an order, and do not merge them into one task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a whole is composed of several units, each unit is built and then checked on its own, and the whole is assembled only after the checks of all units are complete

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that each of several items is produced and then checked on its own, and that a later step for the items happens only if every check succeeds, while items with a failed check must be reworked: Model one check task per item, each labelled with the check the description names for that item, placed after that item's production step and not merged into a single combined check. After the last check, model one decision gateway whose label asks whether all checks passed. Its success outcome leads to the later combined step, and its failure outcome leads to the rework task the description states, with the flow returning to the item's production step. Do not omit per-item checks, and do not let the success path skip the gateway.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that each of several items is produced and then checked on its own, and that a later step for the items happens only if every check succeeds, while items with a failed check must be reworked

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that materials are given to a group of people who then perform a sorting step on them before the next activity: Model the hand-over of the materials as its own manual task, placed after the activity that obtains the materials and before the group's sorting activity, connected by sequence flows. Do not omit this hand-over task or fold it into the group's sorting activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that materials are given to a group of people who then perform a sorting step on them before the next activity

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that materials or items are handed over to a group of people who then carry out a stated activity on them, so the handover is a step before that activity: Model the handover as its own manual task, performed by people and not by a system, placed after the step that prepares the materials and before the group's activity. Model the group's activity as a separate following task. Do not omit the handover, and do not fold it into the label of the group's activity task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that materials or items are handed over to a group of people who then carry out a stated activity on them, so the handover is a step before that activity

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a decision after a review is approved or not approved, and that the approved outcome is followed by a named action performed on the item before the process moves on to a later stage: Model the decision as an exclusive gateway with one conditional outgoing flow per outcome. On the approved flow, place a task that names the approved action, and connect that task to the next stage, so the approved path does not skip the action. On the not-approved flow, return to the earlier stage named in the description. Do not connect the decision gateway directly to the later stage, and do not omit the approval action task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that when a check on a unit or a supply fails (for example a supply is exhausted, or a verification outcome is not positive), a corrective activity is performed, and the process then continues only after that check is repeated

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that a set of separate items each go through the same ordered sequence of steps (for example, one step and then a check of that item), the items are independent of each other, and a later step proceeds only after every item has completed its sequence: Model a parallel gateway that forks into one branch per item. Place that item's ordered steps in sequence within its own branch, so each branch keeps the step order stated for the item and each step is its own task. Close all branches with one matching parallel gateway placed before the later step. Do not collapse the per-item steps into a single task, do not chain the items one after another, and do not use an exclusive gateway to join branches that must all complete.
